title.en: Unit 2 · Differentiation — Definition and Fundamental Properties

body.en: Unit 2 · Differentiation — Definition and Fundamental Properties covers essential College Board AP Calculus AB competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Limit Definition & Power, Product, Quotient Rules

body.en: Calculate derivatives using \(f'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\), power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}[x^n] = nx^{n-1}\), and basic trig derivatives.

Product Rule: \((fg)' = f'g + fg'\). Quotient Rule: \((f/g)' = \frac{f'g - fg'}{g^2}\). \(\frac{d}{dx}[\sin x] = \cos x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}[\cos x] = -\sin x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}[e^x] = e^x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}[\ln x] = \frac{1}{x}\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Find the derivative of \(f(x) = x^3 e^x\).

solution.en: Apply Product Rule: \[ f'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}[x^3]e^x + x^3\frac{d}{dx}[e^x] = 3x^2 e^x + x^3 e^x = \mathbf{x^2 e^x (3 + x)}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Tangent Line Equations & Differentiability vs Continuity

body.en: Write tangent lines \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) and recognize that differentiability implies continuity (corners, cusps, vertical tangents fail differentiability).

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Write the equation of the line tangent to the graph of \(f(x) = \frac{2x}{x+1}\) at the point where \(x = 1\).

solution.en: Find \(f(1)\): \(f(1) = 2/2 = 1\), so the point is \((1, 1)\). Use Quotient Rule: \[ f'(x) = \frac{2(x+1) - 2x(1)}{(x+1)^2} = \frac{2}{(x+1)^2}. \] At \(x = 1\): \(m = f'(1) = 2/4 = 1/2\). Tangent line equation: \[ y - 1 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1) \implies \mathbf{y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Recognizing Limit Definitions of Derivatives

body.en: Identify expressions representing derivatives at a point, such as \(\lim_{h\to 0} \frac{\ln(2+h) - \ln(2)}{h} = \frac{d}{dx}[\ln x]_{x=2} = \frac{1}{2}\).

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the limit without using L'Hospital's Rule: \(\lim_{x\to \pi/4} \frac{\tan(x) - 1}{x - \pi/4}\).

solution.en: This is the alternate limit definition of the derivative: \[ \lim_{x\to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} = f'(c) \] where \(f(x) = \tan(x)\) and \(c = \pi/4\). Since \(f'(x) = \sec^2(x)\): \[ f'(\pi/4) = \sec^2(\pi/4) = (\sqrt{2})^2 = \mathbf{2}. \]
